title: Reject PR3019 fixed P104 matching with a monotone relay cut
body:
PR3019's matching passes its independent-contact support test but cannot implement the additive correction under the stated monotone frame contract. The relay `139 -> 91 -> 83` forces vector 113 into helper 91's frame before requiring that frame inside a plane excluding 113. At least 45 required coefficients at Y40 are therefore impossible, including the added coefficient `C[40,1]=1/2`.

Only helper 91 needs a consistent flag; the other 207 remain relaxed. All 9,765 choices reject: 477 miss 45 dependencies and 9,288 miss 46. A separate implementation reconstructs the exact local contact cut directly from frozen JSON, without importing the primary checker or predecessor code. [Proof and scope](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5b1a7939393ef2778ec058ee8367cdad52c86fb3/research/p104-fixed-matching-flag-consistency/PROOF.md), [reproduction and credit](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5b1a7939393ef2778ec058ee8367cdad52c86fb3/research/p104-fixed-matching-flag-consistency/README.md), [canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2245#discussioncomment-18981114).

Local registered CPython 3.12 replay and optimized CPython 3.14 checks pass, including 8 behavioral groups, an actual nonnested relay that restores all 4,992 relaxed paths, source/receipt corruption and read-only Git-free exports. Exact committed bytes match all 11 package files and 3 external inputs. Hosted CI is separate.

This rejects one frozen matching for the correction increment `I-G/2`. It inherits the original channel's `G/2` contract and proves no new lifetime minimum, supplier admission or kappa. Different matchings and changed access contracts remain open. Credit Nick Petalas/PR3019/3013/2996/2981/2920, Arham Tahir/PR2997 and the retained P104 geometry/native/compiler lineage. Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and two internal mathematical specialist implementations; Apache-2.0. No independent human or formal-kernel review claimed.
